Associate Professors WOT and Professors WOT hold indefinite appointments that align with a 12-month service period (July 1-June 30). Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences Department/Area Position Description The Keutsch Group is seeking a Postdoctoral Fellow in Atmospheric Science. The successful candidate will conduct laboratory experiments investigating heterogeneous halogen and nitrogen chemistry on organic and biomass-burning aerosols under stratospheric conditions. The research will focus on determining reactive uptake rates and other parameters needed to characterize these heterogeneous processes. Experimental results will be integrated into models of stratospheric chemistry to quantify their effects on stratospheric composition, with particular emphasis on ozone. The postdoctoral fellow will also participate in planned stratospheric airborne field campaigns, including the collection of aerosol samples for subsequent offline microanalysis. The position will provide opportunities to work across laboratory, field, and modeling components of a larger collaborative research program. The postdoctoral fellow will be part of a multidisciplinary team at Harvard and will collaborate with research groups outside Harvard involved in the broader project. The successful candidate will also contribute to the mentoring of graduate and/or undergraduate students participating in the research. Basic Qualifications Doctorate in atmospheric science, atmospheric chemistry, or a closely related field by the time the appointment begins. Additional Qualifications A strong record of experimental research is preferred. Experience with experimental methods is desirable as is experience with airborne field campaigns and/or measurements conducted in aircraft-based research environments. Knowledge of stratospheric chemistry, including processes affecting stratospheric ozone, is preferred. Experience working collaboratively as part of a multidisciplinary research team is desirable. The Department of Pediatrics at the University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) John Sealy School of Medicine in Galveston is seeking a full-time Pediatric Developmental Behavioral Pediatrician the rank of Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor. This is a unique opportunity to join a nationally recognized academic health system and a collaborative team of clinicians and researchers.
This position offers the opportunity to engage in clinical care, contribute to the education of pediatric residents and medical students, and develop a productive funded research program.
Position Overview:
This full-time academic role combines clinical care, teaching and research within a collaborative health system. The successful candidate will:
• Join a multidisciplinary team to support the institutional clinical, educational and research missions.
• Provide comprehensive pediatric outpatient psychological assessment and intervention services to children and families.
• Teach and mentor medical students, residents, and fellows.
Qualifications:
Required
• M.D. or D.O. degree from an LCME or COCA accredited medical school.
• Completion of an ACGME-accredited Pediatric Residency.
• Board Certification in American Board of Professional Psychology.
• Ability to obtain an unrestricted State of Texas Physician License.
• Current U.S. DEA Practitioner registration.
• U.S. Citizenship or Employment Authorization to work in the U.S.
• Demonstrated commitment to patient care and medical education.
• Demonstrated clinical and/or basic science research productivity.
Income Package:
Salary will be commensurate with academic rank, qualifications, and experience. The position includes a provision for dedicated research time .
In addition, UTMB offers a superior benefits package, including an excellent retirement program and a relocation allowance.
Living and Working in the Galveston, Texas area:
The Galveston to Houston area offers a unique combination of urban convenience, coastal living, and rich history, and just a short drive from Houston, the 4th largest city in the U.S. Affordable housing, proximity to major highways, and exceptional healthcare and school systems provide an ideal living environment for medical professionals.
The UTMB main campus is in Galveston, a vibrant island city known for beautiful beaches, historic architecture, and thriving tourism and healthcare sectors. Residents and visitors enjoy a relaxed lifestyle with a wide range of recreational opportunities, including boating, fishing, and festivals. Learn more about Galveston by visiting this link: Things to do in Galveston.
About UTMB Health:
The University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB Health) is a nationally recognized academic health center with a proud history of advancing education, research, and patient care. UTMB was established in 1891 as the first medical school in Texas. In 1924, UTMB established the first Department of Pediatrics in Texas.
UTMB has grown into a nearly $4 billion health science center that includes five hospitals, a robust network of outpatient clinics, and five schools — Medicine, Nursing, Health Professions, Graduate Biomedical Sciences, and Public and Population Health.
UTMB is home to more than 15 research centers, 6 institutes, and the Galveston National Laboratory — one of only two university-based BSL-4 labs in the nation. In 2025, UTMB ranked 62nd of 151 medical school in NIH funding; research funding has increased by 20% over the past five years. UTMB has been recognized as a top performer in Vizient’s 2025 Bernard A. Birnbaum Quality and Accountability Awards for Pediatric Hospital Services, ranking 7th out of 98 medical centers measured nationwide. UTMB offers healthcare professionals the opportunity to contribute to an innovative, mission-driven environment with a lasting impact on the health of Texas and beyond.

Position description The Benioff Ocean Science Laboratory seeks a highly motivated postdoctoral scholar to conduct field research on gray whale biology and ecology in the San Francisco Bay. In the last five years, an increasing number of gray whales (Eschrichtius robustus) appear to be using the Bay as a migratory stopover during their 12,000 mile journey between Mexico and the Arctic. Marine mammal biologists have observed gray whales feeding and/or attempting to feed in the Bay, a departure from past migratory behavior that is not yet well understood and that puts whales in closer contact with human activity and often at greater risk of harm, including increased risk of ship strikes. This research is targeted at answering some of the core ecological questions related to understanding how and why gray whales are currently using the Bay and what effects this use of Bay habitats has on the whales themselves. Though specific research questions may be defined in collaboration with the successful candidate, example questions that may be addressed include: ● What San Francisco Bay habitats are most important to gray whales and what are the general temporal and spatial patterns of use? ● What specific benthic prey resources are the whales using in the Bay? ● What is the nutritional value of these prey resources and is there physiological evidence that gray whales are benefiting from access to these food resources? ● To which toxicological risks could gray whales be exposed by feeding upon prey sources within the Bay? ● How may the feeding ecology of gray whales be shaping the ecology of the Bay itself? The specific methodologies will be shaped collaboratively with the successful candidate based on their background and interests and the expertise of project principal investigators. These methods may include: ● benthic ecology surveys and sampling ● direct vessel-based observation of gray whale feeding ecology within the San Francisco Bay ● uncrewed aerial systems surveys ● review and analysis of long-term datasets curated by Bay monitoring and management agencies ● lab-based analyses of whale tissue ● prey energetic analyses ● molecular/eDNA diet analysis ● stable isotope analysis ● contaminant sampling ● acoustic benthic mapping ● ecological modeling The postdoc will work closely with collaborators at UC Santa Barbara, UC Berkeley, the Marine Mammal Center, and additional stakeholders. The postdoc will take the lead in defining field and lab research plans, managing the logistics for accomplishment of this plan, collection and analysis of all data, publishing the results in peer-reviewed journal(s), and communicating about the research with relevant stakeholders. The field research work will be conducted primarily in the Bay Area during the gray whale field season (approximately Jan-May). However, the on-site work location for the remainder of the season will be UC Santa Barbara. Salary is competitive and commensurate with the applicant's qualifications and experience. The Department of Pediatrics at the University of Texas Medical Branch (UTMB) John Sealy School of Medicine is seeking an outstanding physician-scientist in Pediatric Nephrology to join our growing academic program. The position is open at the Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor level, commensurate with experience and academic accomplishments.
This is an exceptional opportunity for a pediatric nephrologist with a strong commitment to research, clinical excellence, education, and academic leadership to develop and lead an independent research program while providing high-quality care to children with kidney disease.
The Opportunity
The successful candidate will join a collaborative Pediatric Nephrology program providing comprehensive care for children with renal disorders across UTMB's clinical network, including Galveston and League City. The division provides care for children with a broad spectrum of kidney conditions, including hypertension, chronic kidney disease, congenital and acquired renal disorders, and disorders of bladder and urinary function.
The physician-scientist will have the opportunity to:
• Develop and sustain an independent, externally funded research program in pediatric nephrology or a related area.
• Pursue innovative basic, translational, clinical, or population health research relevant to kidney health in children.
• Collaborate with investigators across Pediatrics, Internal Medicine, the Graduate School of Biomedical Sciences, and UTMB's research centers and institutes.
• Mentor medical students, residents, and junior faculty in research and scholarly activities.
• Participate in clinical care within Pediatric Nephrology, with opportunities for both inpatient and outpatient practice.
• Contribute to the continued development and expansion of Pediatric Nephrology clinical and research programs at UTMB.
• Participate in teaching and educational activities for medical students and pediatric residents.
• Provide academic and clinical leadership commensurate with rank and experience.
Research Environment
UTMB offers a highly collaborative academic environment with extensive opportunities for interdisciplinary investigation. The institution has more than 10 research centers and three institutes, as well as the Galveston National Laboratory, providing opportunities for collaboration across basic, translational, and clinical research programs. UTMB is currently ranked among the nation's leading academic institutions in NIH research funding.
We are particularly interested in candidates whose research complements or expands existing expertise in areas such as:
• Pediatric kidney disease and chronic kidney disease
• Hypertension and cardiovascular-kidney health
• Kidney development and congenital kidney disorders
• Glomerular and tubular diseases
• Acute kidney injury
• Kidney disease biomarkers and precision medicine
• Translational nephrology
• Clinical and outcomes research
• Health disparities and population health
• Innovative approaches to prevention and treatment of pediatric kidney disease
Candidates with established NIH funding or a strong record of obtaining extramural support are especially encouraged to apply. Early-career investigators with strong research potential and a compelling vision for developing an independent program are also encouraged to apply.
The successful candidate will:
• Provide compassionate, evidence-based care to children with kidney disease.
• Participate in inpatient and outpatient Pediatric Nephrology services.
• Teach and mentor learners at multiple levels.
• Develop collaborative research initiatives and pursue extramural funding.
• Publish scholarly work in high-impact peer-reviewed journals.
• Participate in departmental and institutional committees and academic activities.
• Contribute to the strategic growth of Pediatric Nephrology at UTMB.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:
• MD, DO, or equivalent medical degree.
